title: Topics as Proxies for Sociodemographics: How Conversational Context Affects LLM Answers
abstract: arXiv:2606.02776v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: When large language models (LLMs) are used in high-stakes scenarios, such as legal, medical and financial advice, even a single conversation history is enough to drive differences in outcomes between users. Prior work has demonstrated that this results in outcome disparities between sociodemographic groups, with some groups receiving more advantageous outcomes than others. In this work, we demonstrate that LLMs actually struggle to infer user sociodemographics from a single conversation history and that although there are disparities between sociodemographic groups, they are minimal in magnitude. To investigate what is the main driver of disparities between users, we compare user sociodemographics to a range of (psycho)linguistic features of conversations, including conversation topic, emotions, and readability. translated_title: 话题作为社会人口统计特征的代理：对话背景如何影响大语言模型的回答
translated_abstract: 当大语言模型（LLMs）被用于法律、医疗和金融建议等高风险场景时，即使只有一段对话历史也足以导致用户之间结果的差异。先前的研究表明，这会导致社会人口统计群体之间的结果不公平，某些群体获得比其他群体更有利的结果。在本研究中，我们证明LLMs实际上难以从单一对话历史中推断用户的社会人口统计特征，尽管社会人口统计群体之间存在差异，但这些差异在幅度上很小。为了探究用户之间差异的主要驱动因素，我们将用户的社会人口统计特征与一系列对话的（心理）语言学特征进行比较，包括对话话题、情感和可读性。我们发现，在对话背景下，对话话题最能预测LLM生成的建议，这在一定程度上...
tldr: 本文发现对话话题而非用户社会人口统计特征是导致大语言模型回答差异的主要驱动因素，且社会人口统计推断能力有限。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that conversation topics, rather than user sociodemographics, are the primary driver of disparities in LLM-generated responses, while LLMs struggle to infer sociodemographics from single conversations.
